memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “While they watched, He was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight.” -Acts 1:9 .

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
At Christmas, we lovingly remember Jesus in the manger, surrounded by straw, lambs, and cattle. We decorate cribs, sing carols, exchange gifts, wear new clothes, and gather around Christmas trees. Jingle bells ring, Santa images shine, and celebrations multiply. Yet in all this noise, one serious question remains: Where is Jesus now? 

Christ was not born to remain in a manger. The manger was temporary, but the throne is eternal.
Jesus is no longer lying helpless in Bethlehem; He is reigning gloriously in heaven. The child wrapped in swaddling clothes is now the King clothed in majesty. The One once laid in a feeding trough is now seated at the right hand of Father God, far above all rule, authority, and power. Christmas loses its true meaning when we freeze Jesus in infancy and forget His exaltation. We celebrate His birth, but neglect His Lordship.

True Christmas is not about how beautifully we decorate the season, but how deeply we submit to the risen and reigning Christ. Heaven does not celebrate Jesus as a baby; . heaven worships Him as King of kings and Lord of lords. When we lift Jesus from the manger to the throne in our hearts, Christmas becomes revival, not tradition. Christ is not asking for a cradle; He is demanding, the throne of our lives.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “If Christ is not Lord of all, He is not Lord at all.” - A W Tozer.

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, forgive us for remembering Your birth
and ignoring Your throne. We crown You not just as the Child of Bethlehem, but as the King of Heaven.
Reign over our hearts, homes, and lives. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Do not keep Jesus in the manger of sentiment.
Lift Him to the throne of surrender. Celebrate Christ, not as a memory, but as your reigning King.
